BURSEVI:v10p87#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p87#2/r1.speaker: الرغب
BURSEVI:v10p87#2/r1.claim: Al-Rāghib defines exception as wording that removes part of a preceding general statement or removes a ruling from its stated form.
BURSEVI:v10p87#2/r1.anchor: قال الرغب الاستثناء إيراد لفظ يقضتي رفع بعض

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p432/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p432/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p432/r1.claim: Although exegetes unanimously take the phrase to mean they omitted ‘if God wills,’ Islahi rejects that reading: the construction is unsuitable, and istithnāʾ is not explicit enough without contextual evidence.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p432/r1.anchor: Although all the exegetes are unanimous in this interpretation, I personally am not convinced of it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p432/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p432/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p432/r2.claim: He reads istithnāʾ literally: they swore to take all the fruit and leave none for the poor, rejecting a customary charitable gleaning practice also stated in Leviticus.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p432/r2.anchor: what they swore was that they would pick all the fruit and leave nothing for the poor

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p432/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p432/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p432/r3.claim: The oath about leaving nothing emphasizes the same stinginess as Quraysh leaders’ forbidding good, especially Abū Lahab and his associates.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p432/r3.anchor: the picture of the stinginess of Abū Lahab and his associates

FARRA:v3p174/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p174/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p174/r3.claim: After their father's death, the sons decided to stop giving because their dependents had grown and wealth shrunk; they planned to harvest in the late-night darkness so the poor would receive nothing.
FARRA:v3p174/r3.anchor: فإنا ندع ذلك، ثم تآمروا أن يصرموا في سدف: في ظلمة- باقية من الليل

FARRA:v3p174/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p174/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p174/r6.claim: The justest brother's call to tasbih means to make an exception by saying إن شاء الله, as in the instruction to remember God after forgetting.
FARRA:v3p174/r6.anchor: ألم أقل لكم لولا تسبحون؟ فالتسبيح هاهنا في معنى الاستثناء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r2.claim: One account places the garden in Yemen near Ṣanʿāʾ; its owner paid God's due, but his sons withheld it after inheriting and the garden was destroyed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r2.anchor: كانت بأرض اليمن بالقرب منهم قريبا من صنعاء لرجل كان يؤدي حق الله منها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r3.claim: Another account locates it at Ṣurawān near Ṣanʿāʾ after Jesus; the owner left poor neighbors dates and grapes missed by harvesters, but his sons decided to stop sharing because they had dependents.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r3.anchor: وكان صاحبها ينزل للمساكنين ما أخطأه المنجل وما في أسفل الأكراس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r4.claim: The sons swore to harvest early in darkness and secretly, keeping the poor from their customary share; the oath's response predicts that they would cut the crop.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r4.anchor: فحلفوا ليصرمنها مصبحين في السدف خفية من المساكين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r5.claim: Mujāhid explains “they made no exception” as not saying إن شاء الله; al-Zamakhsharī follows him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: معناه: لا يقولون إن شاء الله، بل عزموا على ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains why saying “if God wills” is called an exception: it has the practical force of not doing something unless God wills.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r6.anchor: لأنه يؤدي مؤدى الاستثناء من حيث إن معنى قولك: لأخرجن إن شاء الله،

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p479/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p479/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p479/r1.claim: They swore they would gather the garden's fruit in the morning and did not make an exception.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p479/r1.anchor: {إذ أقسموا ليصرمنها مصبحين * ولا يستثنون} أي حلفوا ليجذن ثمرها صباحا؛ ولم يستثنوا.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#2/r1.claim: One reading is that they did not say inshaAllah; although that is technically a condition, its effect matches an exception.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#2/r1.anchor: ولا يقولون إن شاء الله تعالى وتسميته استثناء مع أنه شرط من حيث أن مؤداه مؤدى الإستثناء

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#2/r2.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#2/r2.claim: The Imam derives the literal sense of an exception from restraint or turning back: a condition prevents an oath from taking effect.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#2/r2.anchor: وقال الإمام أصل الإستثناء من الثني وهو الكف والرد في التقييد بالشرط رد لانعقاد ذلك اليمين

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, they did not turn back from their plan to deprive the poor; the syntax apparently links the phrase to their swearing.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#2/r3.anchor: وقيل أي ولا يثنون عما هموا به من منع المساكين

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#2/r4.claim: Using the present tense instead of the expected past evokes their failure to make an exception and signals their error.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#2/r4.anchor: وفي العدول إلى المضارع نوع تعبير وتنبيه على مكان خطئهم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#2/r5.speaker: في الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#2/r5.claim: Al-Kashf construes the clause as a circumstantial phrase: they were in the state of not making an exception.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#2/r5.anchor: وفي الكشف هو حال أي غير مستثنين

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#2/r6.claim: A further interpretation is that they excluded no share for the poor as their father had done; this may attach to their harvesting oath or its timing.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#2/r6.anchor: وقيل المعنى ولا يستثنون حصة المساكين كما كان يخرج أبوهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195/r1.claim: They did not make an exception by saying ‘if God wills.’
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195/r1.anchor: {ولا يستثنون} ولا يقولون إن شاء الله.

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:18-22/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:18-22/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:18-22/r1.claim: They did not say God willing; this is called exception because it excludes a condition, or because willing harvest and not harvesting until God wills are equivalent formulations.
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:18-22/r1.anchor: { ولا يستثنون } ولا يقولون إن شاء الله، وإنما سماه استثناء لما فيه من الإخراج

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:18-22/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:18-22/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:18-22/r2.claim: Alternatively, they failed to reserve the poor’s share, as their father had done.
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:18-22/r2.anchor: أو { ولا يستثنون } حصة المساكين كما كان يخرج أبوهم

BINTSHATI:v2p63/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r2.claim: The apparent story is that the garden owners planned to harvest everything at dawn and leave nothing; the author rejects the gloss that they merely omitted saying in shāʾ Allāh.
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r2.anchor: وظاهر النص، أن خطيئتهم التي أخذوا بها، هي التصميم على صرم جنتهم خفية

BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.claim: Exegetes elaborate the garden story: it belonged to a righteous man who left it to his people and town; reports place it in Yemen near Ṣanʿāʾ, Abyssinia, or among the People of Scripture.
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.anchor: أن هذه الجنة كانت لرجل صالح، حدودا قومه وبلده فقيل إنه من أهل اليمن

NAHHAS:v5p9/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p9/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p9/r15.claim: They were censured for not saying 'if God wills': an intended action may be prevented, making the speaker a liar unless he qualifies it.
NAHHAS:v5p9/r15.anchor: ولا يقولون إن شاء الله فذموا بهذا لأن الإنسان إذا قال لأفعلن كذا لم يأمن

BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r5.claim: Not making an exception means they neither said inshallah nor used another phrase returning the matter to God's will; such an exception removes some of the oath's absolute force.

DURR-FULL:v8p251/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p251/r1.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR-FULL:v8p251/r1.claim: Abu Salih says their exception was the phrase Subhan Allah.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r20.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r20.claim: ولا يستثنون can mean they did not pause, or turn back from their decision to exclude the poor.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r20.anchor: وقوله تعالى: ولا يستثنون ولا يتوقفون في ذلك، أو ولا ينثنون عن رأي منع المساكين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r21.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r21.claim: Mujahid says they did not say إن شاء الله and resolved as if they controlled the outcome.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r21.anchor: وقال مجاهد معناه: لا يقولون إن شاء الله، بل عزموا على ذلك عزم من يملك أمره

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p335#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p335#2/r1.speaker: الأكثرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p335#2/r1.claim: They did not say in shāʾ Allāh when making their vow.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p335#2/r1.anchor: أحدهما لا يقولون إن شاء الله قاله الأكثرون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p335#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p335#2/r2.speaker: عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p335#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, they did not set aside the poor people's due.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p335#2/r2.anchor: والثاني لا يستثنون حق المساكين قاله عكرمة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p195/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p195/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p195/r2.claim: The heirs swore to harvest at dawn so that no poor person or petitioner would learn of the crop and receive charity; they made no exception in their oath.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p195/r2.anchor: حلفوا فيما بينهم ليجذن ثمرها ليلا لئلا يعلم بهم فقير ولا سائل

JISHUMI:v10p7031/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7031/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7031/r7.claim: An exception removes a member from a general class; an exception by God's will instead lifts the ruling of the statement, such as saying unless God wills to prevent or enable me.
JISHUMI:v10p7031/r7.anchor: والاستثناء: إخراج بعض من كل، لولاه لدخل فيه

JISHUMI:v10p7036/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7036/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7036/r1.claim: The owners are blamed for denying the poor their due, swearing to do so, and omitting an exception; this supports requiring an exception when speaking about the future, since one cannot be sure the statement will come true.
JISHUMI:v10p7036/r1.anchor: ذمهم على منع الحق، وذمهم على القسم عليه، وذمهم على ترك الاستثناء

JISHUMI:v10p7036/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7036/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7036/r2.claim: Intending an evil act is itself blameworthy: they were punished for the resolve even before committing the wrong, and actually taking property and denying rights is worse.
JISHUMI:v10p7036/r2.anchor: أن العزم على القبيح قبيح؛ لأنهم عوقبوا على عزمهم من غير منع وظلم بالمنع

SAMIN-DURR:68:18/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:18/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:18/r1.claim: ولا يستثنون begins a new sentence; a circumstantial parse is weak because negated present verbs do not take an introductory wāw, and no hidden topic is needed.

SAMIN-DURR:68:18/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:18/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:18/r2.claim: لا يستثنون may mean they did not reconsider their resolve to withhold, or that they did not say إن شاء الله; calling it an exception is justified because the condition and exception mean the same.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r7.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r7.claim: Not making an exception means that they excluded no share for the poor.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r7.anchor: أحدها : لا يستثنون من المساكين , قاله عكرمة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r8.speaker: أبو صالح
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r8.claim: Not making an exception may mean that their exception would have been the words سبحان ربنا.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r8.anchor: الثاني : استثناؤهم قول سبحان ربنا , قاله أبو صالح .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r9.claim: The omitted exception may mean saying إن شاء الله.

MUQATIL:68:17-27/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:68:17-27/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:68:17-27/r2.claim: They did not make an exception by saying God willing; God heard this, then sent fire from heaven that night and burned the garden black.
MUQATIL:68:17-27/r2.anchor: { ولا يستثنون } [آية: 18] فيقولون: إن شاء الله، فسمع الله تعالى قولهم فبعث نارا من السماء

NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#6/r1.claim: They did not say “if God wills”; this is called an exception although formally it is a condition, since both expressions mean that the act occurs only if God wills.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#6/r1.anchor: ولا يقولون إن شاء الله وسمى استثناء وإن كان شرطا صورة

QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r5.claim: “They made no exception” means they did not say “if God wills.”
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r5.anchor: أي ولم يقولوا إن شاء الله

QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r9.speaker: أبو صالح
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r9.claim: Abu Salih says their formula of exception was “Glory be to God, our Lord.”

QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r10.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r10.claim: Ikrima interprets their failure to make an exception as failing to exempt the poor’s due from their plan.

RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r6.claim: Most commentators say they did not make an exception by saying 'if God wills' because they were overconfident they could harvest; another view says they refused to set aside the poor's usual share.
RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r6.anchor: فالأكثرون أنهم إنما لم يستثنوا بمشيئة الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r7.claim: Istithnāʾ derives from th-n-y, turning something back: adding 'unless God wills' suspends the oath's certainty.
RAZI-FULL:v30p77#2/r7.anchor: وأصل هذا كله من الثني وهو الكف والرد

STUDYQURAN:68:17/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r2.speaker: Bg, IK, Z
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r2.claim: “Made no exception” can mean the brothers did not say “If God wills,” showing they relied on themselves rather than God.
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r2.anchor: Made no exception is taken to indicate that they did not say, “If God wills” (Bg, IK, Z)

STUDYQURAN:68:17/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r3.claim: The brothers’ failure to make an exception indicates self-reliance rather than trust in God.
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r3.anchor: and thus trusted in themselves rather than in God (R)

STUDYQURAN:68:17/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r4.claim: Alternatively, “made no exception” can mean that they left no part of the harvest for the poor.
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r4.anchor: It could also be a reference to the harvest, indicating that they left no portion for the poor

ASAD-NOTES:68:14#n12/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:14#n12/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:68:14#n12/r1.claim: They planned without saying 'if God wills'; this is the parable's first lesson and links it to the question about their wealth in vv.14-15.
ASAD-NOTES:68:14#n12/r1.anchor: which points to the first lesson to be derived from this parable

TAB-FULL:v23p171/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p171/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p171/r1.claim: God tested the Quraysh disbelievers as He tested the garden owners: they swore to harvest at dawn and did not say “if God wills.”

TAB-FULL:v23p171/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p171/r2.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v23p171/r2.claim: ʿIkrima says the owners were Ethiopians whose father fed the poor from his garden; after he died, his sons called him foolish and vowed to exclude the poor.
TAB-FULL:v23p171/r2.anchor: هم ناس من الحبشة كانت لأبيهم جنة كان يطعم المساكين منها

TAB-FULL:v23p171/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p171/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p171/r3.claim: Qatāda says the garden belonged to a charitable old man; his sons opposed his charity and, after his death, set out to keep poor people away.
TAB-FULL:v23p171/r3.anchor: كانت الجنة لشيخ، وكان يتصدق، فكان بنوه ينهونه عن الصدقة

TABATABAI:68:17-21/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:17-21/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:17-21/r7.claim: The garden owners agreed at night to harvest in the morning; not making an exception means they relied on themselves and outward causes without acknowledging God's will.
TABATABAI:68:17-21/r7.anchor: وكأنهم ائتمروا وتشاوروا ليلا فعزموا على الصرم صبيحة ليلتهم

TABATABAI:68:20-28/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:20-28/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:20-28/r1.claim: Another possible sense of not making an exception is that they set aside no share of the fruit for the poor.
TABATABAI:68:20-28/r1.anchor: أو المعنى قالوا وهم لا يعزلون نصيبا من ثمارهم للفقراء والمساكين

TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas tells of a father who always gave each rightful person a share, then five sons who planned to keep an unusually abundant harvest from Muslim poor; four agreed and the moderate brother objected.
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r11.anchor: فقال ابن عباس فوالله الذي لا إله إلا هو هذا أنور في كتاب الله من الشمس الضاحية

THALABI:v10p16/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p16/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p16/r7.claim: Aqsumu means they swore, yasrim means to cut or harvest its fruit, and musbihin means at dawn before the poor knew.
THALABI:v10p16/r7.anchor: قوله تعالى: إذ أقسموا حلفوا، ليصرمنها لتجديها ولتقطيع ثمرها، مصبحين إذ أصبحوا قبل أن يعلم المساكين

THALABI:v10p16/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p16/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p16/r8.claim: They did not say insha Allah when they planned their harvest.
THALABI:v10p16/r8.anchor: ولا يستثنون لا يقولون إن شاء الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p96#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p96#2/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p96#2/r1.claim: The exegetes say they did not say if God wills.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p96#2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {ولا يستثنون} يقولون: إن شاء الله. هذا قول جماعة # المفسرين (¬1). ويقال: حلف فلان يمينا ليس فيها ثنيا ولا ثنوى ولا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p96#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p96#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p96#2/r2.claim: Several forms describe an oath without exception; they derive from ثني, to restrain or turn back, because exception returns the oath to God's will.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p96#2/r2.anchor: الثني وهو الكف والرد (¬2)، وذلك أن الحالف إذا قال: والله لأفعلن كذا إلا أن يشاء الله غيره فقد رد ما قاله بمشيئة الله غيره.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:17-21/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:17-21/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:17-21/r2.claim: They did not make an exception by saying “if God wills.”
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:17-21/r2.anchor: { ولا يستثنون } ولا يقولون إن شاء الله

ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r12.claim: They made no exception such as “if God wills,” if they reached morning safely, or if no accident befell them, because their overconfident resolve did not consider failing their vow or a reversal of fortune.
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r12.anchor: “inşaallah, Allah izin verirse” yahut “sağ sâlim sabaha çıkarsak, bir kazâ ve âfete uğramazsak” gibi bir şart

ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r13.claim: Alternatively, their failure to make an exception means they wanted to give nothing to anyone else and did not consider that anyone besides them might harvest the garden.
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r13.anchor: Yahut kendilerinden başka kimseye bir şey vermek istemiyorlar, onu kendilerinden başka birisinin kesebileceğini hesâba almıyorlardı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r4.speaker: Müfessirlerin çoğunluğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r4.claim: Most commentators say the garden owners resolved what they would do the next day without saying 'if God wills.'
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r4.anchor: Müfessirlerin çoğunluğu 18. âyeti, “Bahçe sahipleri ‘Allah izin verirse’ demeden ertesi gün yapacakları iş hakkında karar verdiler” şeklinde açıklamışlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r5.speaker: bazı yorumlar
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r5.claim: An alternative interpretation is that they made no provision for the poor's share.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r5.anchor: “yoksulların payını ayırmaksızın” şeklinde de bir yorum vardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r6.claim: When intending future action, people should say inshaallah because human will and power alone cannot make an event occur; God's will is also necessary.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r6.anchor: Gelecekte bir işi yapmaya niyet ederken “inşaallah” diyerek işi Allah’ın iradesine bağlamak gerekir
